land.text: Waalo on the lower Senegal river from Saint-Louis inland to Lac de Guiers (the page names the lower Senegal valley, Awlil, Saint-Louis, Nder and Bethio but gives no outline; the gazetteer's Saint-Louis region stands for it)

successors.note: "The French finally conquered the kingdom in 1855" (Waalo page); Faidherbe's column burned Nder after the battle of Dioubouldy on 25 February 1855 (Ndaté Yalla Mbodj page).

capitals.name: Nder
capitals.note: Ndaté Yalla "was crowned Lingeer of Waalo at Nder" on 1 October 1846 and Nder was burned in February 1855. The Waalo page gives the capital sequence Ndiourbel, Ndiangué, Nder with no dates; the point is the researcher's approximation on the west shore of Lac de Guiers, not on the page.

rulers.name: Ndaté Yalla Mbodj
rulers.title: lingeer
rulers.note: Crowned 1 October 1846 at Nder; the Waalo page gives the last king as Mbeu Mbody Maalik, 1840-1855, in its list.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Waalo row). The page: "associated with the rule of the first king" Ndiadiane Ndiaye "in 1287" (historians debate the date); the lower Senegal valley, Awlil, Saint-Louis, Nder, Bethio, with the Moorish emirates to the north, Cayor to the south and Jolof to the east. No outline is given, so the gazetteer region Saint-Louis stands for it. Waalo was a vassal of Jolof from about 1350 and paid symbolic tribute to 1715; that status is in the jolof-empire dossier.

ledger.note: 1287: Waalo is founded under the semi-legendary Ndiadiane Ndiaye. Page: "associated with the rule of the first king" Ndiaye "in 1287" and "historians debate the exact date"; the infobox gives 1287 as the start.

ledger.note: February 1855: the French take Waalo. Page: "the French finally conquered the kingdom in 1855"; at Dioubouldy on 25 February 1855 the French defeated the combined Waalo and Trarza armies and burned Nder, which the queen had abandoned (Ndaté Yalla Mbodj page, which also gives 31 January 1855 elsewhere and flags it).

ledger.note: February 1855: the kingdom ends. "The Queen remained in Cayor until her death in 1860" (Ndaté Yalla Mbodj page; the infobox gives 1860 or 1856).

wars.name: Cayor-Waalo war

zones.text: Waalo on the lower Senegal river from Saint-Louis inland to Lac de Guiers (the page names the lower Senegal valley, Awlil, Saint-Louis, Nder and Bethio but gives no outline; the gazetteer's Saint-Louis region stands for it)

wars.outcome: Cayor won. "In 1762, Naatago appropriated Cayor's payments"; he invaded two years later and in 1765 "the Damel of Cayor counterattacked, armed with English guns," and defeated Waalo.
wars.note: Only 1762 and 1765 are on the page; the invasion year (1764) is inferred from "two years later".

wars.name: French conquest of Waalo

zones.text: Waalo on the lower Senegal river from Saint-Louis inland to Lac de Guiers (the page names the lower Senegal valley, Awlil, Saint-Louis, Nder and Bethio but gives no outline; the gazetteer's Saint-Louis region stands for it)

wars.outcome: Faidherbe (governor from 1854) left Saint-Louis in February 1855 with about 450 French soldiers and 400 volunteers; on 25 February 1855 at Dioubouldy the French beat the combined Waalo and Trarza armies and burned Nder. Waalo ceased to exist; the queen took refuge in Cayor.
wars.note: The Waalo page says only that "the French finally conquered the kingdom in 1855"; the Ndaté Yalla Mbodj page also gives 31 January 1855 for the conquest and flags it as inconsistent.

certainty.note: The page gives no outline and no dated capital or frontier moves; the Saint-Louis region is a stand-in and omits the Mauritanian bank and the part of the valley the page does not name.

notes:
Waalo, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Waalo, Ndaté Yalla Mbodj.

The vassalage to Jolof (c. 1350 to 1549 de facto, 1715 de jure) is not recorded here: it belongs in the jolof-empire ledger, which carries vassal_start 1360 and vassal_end 1549 with counterpart waalo. The Waalo page has no outline, no date for the capital moves (Ndiourbel, Ndiangué, Nder) and none for the Trarza shift. The Saint-Louis region overlaps the Futa Toro dossier's Podor valley only slightly (that shape is Matam and Gorgol) and covers the lower valley the page names. The Moorish bank and the province of Bethio are not drawn separately. Conquest date: 25 February 1855 (battle) against 31 January 1855 (the same page's other date, flagged), with the infobox end 1855.
Gazetteer: Nder, Ndiourbel, Ndiangué, Awlil, Bethio, Lac de Guiers, Dioubouldy.
